resolutions.researcher_notes: Possible other name for P6899, MountainWest Gas Pipeline. A discovery search found a pipeline called "Overthrust Wamsutter Expansion" and judged it to be part of this row or another name for it. That is a judgment, and there is a chance it is a different pipeline, so check before accepting. Accepting adds the name to the other English names cell and changes nothing else. What the search found: The Wamsutter Expansion Project (Questar Overthrust Pipeline, 77 miles of 36 inch pipe, 750 MMcf/d added, FERC docket CP06-423, completed December 2007) is in the EIA project list for August 2026, sheet Historical Projects (1996-2024), Excel row 471. It is a completed expansion of the Overthrust system. The existing row P6899 (MountainWest Gas Pipeline / Overthrust Gas Pipeline, operating) is recorded at 261 miles and 2,800 MMcf/d, which is far larger than the 77 mile loop and larger than the original system, so it appears to include the 2007 expansion. Treated as part of P6899, not a new row. Not confirmed from the FERC order: web search was unavailable in this run, and the only source is a single EIA release. A person could open the CP06-423 order to confirm that the 77 miles sit inside the 261 miles. Even if it does not, a completed 2007 line is not a new project and would need its own row only if the sheet lacks that pipe. Pages that use the name "Overthrust Wamsutter Expansion": https://www.naturalgasintel.com/?p=62273. Check: Sources say Wamsutter Expansion for Questar Overthrust; none says Overthrust Wamsutter Expansion as a single name. Overthrust is now part of MountainWest.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Possible other name for P7856, Great Basin Gas Transmission Company Pipeline System. A discovery search found a pipeline called "Paiute North Tahoe Lateral" and judged it to be part of this row or another name for it. That is a judgment, and there is a chance it is a different pipeline, so check before accepting. Accepting adds the name to the other English names cell and changes nothing else. The cell already lists: Paiute Pipeline Company Pipeline System. What the search found: EIA Aug 2026 release, Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 66: Paiute North Tahoe Lateral, Paiute Pipeline, completed Dec 1997, 23 mi, 8 and 16 in, 12.78 MMcf/d added, FERC CP94-29, NV and CA. This is a built 1997 lateral of the operating Paiute system (now Great Basin Gas Transmission, about 898 miles). GEM row P7856 (Great Basin Gas Transmission Company Pipeline System, Main Line, other name Paiute Pipeline Company Pipeline System) already represents that operating system. No separate row for a completed 1997 lateral; the other Paiute historical laterals (Elko, Carson, South Tahoe) are likewise not separate rows. If Baird wants completed laterals tracked separately, this one would qualify on length (37 km) but would be a policy ruling, not a discovery finding. Only one source (EIA, one origin) was checked; no FERC order was opened. Pages that use the name "Paiute North Tahoe Lateral": https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-08/CP17-471-000.pdf. Check: FERC page says 'North Tahoe Lateral' (a lateral of the Paiute system, now Great Basin); the exact phrase 'Paiute North Tahoe Lateral' was not seen. This is a lateral, not the whole system.

Possible other name for P6898, MountainWest Gas Pipeline. A discovery search found a pipeline called "Questar Main Line 58 Expansion" and judged it to be part of this row or another name for it. That is a judgment, and there is a chance it is a different pipeline, so check before accepting. Accepting adds the name to the other English names cell and changes nothing else. What the search found: The only source found is the EIA August 2026 release, sheet Historical Projects (1996-2024), Excel row 81, project name Questar Mainline (Line 58) Expansion: completed September 1998, Wyoming to Utah, 41 miles, 20 inch, 84.7 MMcf/d added, FERC CP96-820. The URL passed the verifier with the EIA project name. This is a completed 1998 loop on the operating Questar main line, now MountainWest. The existing row P6898 (MountainWest Gas Pipeline, Main Line, 1868 km) very likely already counts this pipe, so it is classed as matched to P6898 rather than a new row. This match was NOT confirmed: the web search for a second source (FERC order or operator document) hit a session limit and was not run. A reviewer should confirm Line 58 is inside P6898's recorded length; if it is a separate, uncounted segment, it would meet the 25 km length rule (41 mi, about 66 km) as an operating expansion row. Owner would be MountainWest Pipeline; entity_lookup was not completed. No GEM sources used. No page that uses the name "Questar Main Line 58 Expansion" was found, so treat it as unconfirmed. Searched Questar/MountainWest Main Line 58 expansion twice; no loaded page used the name. Check: Possible confusion with Questar Southern System Expansion II (58.6 miles, Main Line 104 area); unconfirmed.
